actions.label_short: Keystone XL rejected as not in the national interest
actions.description: The State Department decided the Keystone XL pipeline would not serve the national interest of the United States, and President Obama agreed with that determination.

sources.title: Statement by the President on the Keystone XL Pipeline

actions.label_short: Crude oil export restriction repealed by statute
actions.description: Public Law 114-113 (H.R. 2029), in the title headed Oil Exports, Safety Valve, and Maritime Security, repeals section 103 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act and bars federal officials from imposing or enforcing a restriction on crude oil exports, with a savings clause for presidential authority under the Constitution and the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

sources.title: Public Law 114-113, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016, sec. 101

actions.label_short: U.S. deposits its acceptance of the Paris Agreement
actions.description: The United States deposited its instrument of acceptance of the Paris Agreement on 3 September 2016, per the depositary's notes.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection: Paris Agreement, status and depositary notifications (note 7)

actions.label_short: Memorandum invites a new Keystone XL application
actions.description: A presidential memorandum invited TransCanada Keystone Pipeline, L.P. to re-submit its application to the State Department for a presidential permit for the Keystone XL pipeline.

sources.title: Construction of the Keystone XL Pipeline (Memorandum of January 24, 2017)

actions.label_short: Executive order on energy independence
actions.description: Executive Order 13783, Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth.

sources.title: Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth

actions.label_short: President announces withdrawal from the Paris Agreement
actions.description: President Trump announced that the United States would withdraw from the Paris Agreement and seek to negotiate re-entry on different terms. The formal notification came on 2019-11-04 (see that row).

sources.title: Statement by President Trump on the Paris Climate Accord

actions.label_short: Presidential permit granted for Keystone XL
actions.description: A presidential permit authorizes TransCanada Keystone Pipeline, L.P. to construct, connect, operate and maintain pipeline facilities at the U.S.-Canada border at Phillips County, Montana; it supersedes the permit dated March 23, 2017.

sources.title: Authorizing TransCanada Keystone Pipeline, L.P., To Construct, Connect, Operate, and Maintain Pipeline Facilities at the International Border of the United States and Canada

actions.label_short: First U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Agreement takes effect
actions.description: The United States notified the Secretary-General of its withdrawal on 4 November 2019; it took effect on 4 November 2020 under article 28.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection: Paris Agreement, status and depositary notifications (note 7)

actions.label_short: Executive order revokes the Keystone XL permit
actions.description: Section 6 of Executive Order 13990 revokes the March 29, 2019 presidential permit for the Keystone XL pipeline.

sources.title: Protecting Public Health and the Environment and Restoring Science To Tackle the Climate Crisis

actions.label_short: Executive order on the climate crisis
actions.description: Executive Order 14008, Tackling the Climate Crisis at Home and Abroad, which cites the instrument of acceptance to rejoin the Paris Agreement.

sources.title: Tackling the Climate Crisis at Home and Abroad

actions.label_short: U.S. rejoins the Paris Agreement
actions.description: The United States deposited its instrument of acceptance on 20 January 2021, per the depositary's notes; the acceptance took effect on February 19, 2021.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection: Paris Agreement, status and depositary notifications (note 7)
United States Rejoins the Paris Agreement on Climate Change: Options for Congress (IF11746)

actions.label_short: SPR release of 50 million barrels authorized
actions.description: At the President's direction DOE made available 50 million barrels of SPR crude: up to 32 million through an exchange and an accelerated 18 million barrels of a congressionally mandated sale, announced in parallel with other major consuming countries.

sources.title: DOE To Make Available A Release Of 50 Million Barrels Of Crude Oil From The Strategic Petroleum Reserve

actions.label_short: SPR sale of up to 180 million barrels authorized
actions.description: President Biden's March 31, 2022 announcement authorized the sale of up to 180 million barrels of SPR crude oil, as DOE's later notice describes it; DOE's history page lists a 180 million barrel emergency sale coordinated through the IEA in 2022.

sources.title: DOE Announces Notice of Sale of Additional Crude Oil From the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (2022-09-19)
History of SPR Releases

actions.label_short: Inflation Reduction Act enacted
actions.description: Public Law 117-169 (H.R. 5376), a reconciliation act whose text includes a clean electricity production credit.

sources.title: Public Law 117-169, Inflation Reduction Act of 2022

actions.label_short: DOE pauses pending non-FTA LNG export decisions
actions.description: DOE announced it would pause determinations on pending applications to export LNG to countries without a free trade agreement while it updated its public-interest analysis; exports already authorized (48 Bcf/d) were unaffected.

sources.title: DOE to Update Public Interest Analysis to Enhance National Security, Achieve Clean Energy Goals and Continue Support for Global Allies

actions.label_short: DOE reports its final SPR refill purchase
actions.description: DOE reported 200 million barrels secured in total at an average $74.75 per barrel: 59 million purchased directly and 140 million through congressional action cancelling mandated sales.

sources.title: Biden-Harris Administration Makes Final Purchase for the Strategic Petroleum Reserve - Secures 200 Million Barrels at a Good Deal for the American Taxpayer

actions.label_short: Executive order: Unleashing American Energy
actions.description: Executive Order 14154, which includes provisions on liquefied natural gas export applications and deepwater ports.

sources.title: Unleashing American Energy

actions.label_short: Executive order declares a national energy emergency
actions.description: Executive Order 14156, Declaring a National Energy Emergency.

sources.title: Declaring a National Energy Emergency

actions.label_short: DOE ends the LNG export pause
actions.description: DOE announced it was ending the LNG pause and returning to regular order, directing its fossil energy office to resume processing pending applications to export LNG to non-FTA countries.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Energy Reverses Biden LNG Pause, Restores Trump Energy Dominance Agenda

actions.label_short: Executive order on the coal industry
actions.description: Executive Order 14261, Reinvigorating America's Beautiful Clean Coal Industry and Amending Executive Order 14241.

sources.title: Reinvigorating America's Beautiful Clean Coal Industry and Amending Executive Order 14241

actions.label_short: Reconciliation law ends wind and solar credits
actions.description: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1) amends section 45Y to terminate the clean electricity production credit for wind and solar facilities.

sources.title: Public Law 119-21, reconciliation act of July 4, 2025

actions.label_short: Second U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Agreement takes effect
actions.description: The United States notified the Secretary-General of its withdrawal on 27 January 2025; it took effect on 27 January 2026. Executive Order 14162, signed 2025-01-20, directed the written notification.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection: Paris Agreement, status and depositary notifications (note 7)
Putting America First in International Environmental Agreements

actions.label_short: SPR emergency exchange of 172 million barrels authorized
actions.description: Secretary of Energy Wright announced a presidentially authorized release of 172 million barrels from the SPR, the U.S. share of a 400 million barrel coordinated IEA action, over about 120 days. It is an exchange: the barrels are to be returned, and DOE stated a plan to replace them with about 200 million barrels within a year.

sources.title: United States to Release 172 Million Barrels of Oil From the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
